learn.title: High availability, scalability, elasticity and agility
objectives: Explain high availability and how SLAs express it.
Work out allowed downtime and simple composite SLAs.
Tell scaling up, down, out and in apart, and explain elasticity.
Name the Azure features that deliver availability and scale: availability zones, availability sets, load balancers, VM Scale Sets and autoscale.
Separate high availability, fault tolerance, disaster recovery and agility.
concepts: High availability
Keeping a service up with minimal downtime, usually stated as an uptime percentage in an SLA.
SLA
Microsoft's commitment for a service's uptime or connectivity. If it's missed, customers can claim service credits.
Composite SLA
For services that all must work, multiply their SLAs. The result is lower than any single one.
Scalability
Adjusting resources to match load, manually or automatically.
Vertical scaling
Up or down: change the size of one resource (CPU, RAM).
Horizontal scaling
Out or in: change the number of instances.
Elasticity
Automatic scaling in both directions as demand changes.
Agility
Creating, changing and removing resources quickly.
Availability zones
Separate datacenters in one region. Spreading instances across zones protects against a datacenter failure.
VM Scale Sets
A group of identical, load-balanced VMs whose count can autoscale.
comparisons: Up = bigger machine (often brief downtime, hardware ceiling). Out = more machines (needs a load balancer, no single-machine ceiling).
HA keeps a service running through component failures. DR restores service after a major event, often in another region.
Set = separate racks (fault domains) inside one datacenter. Zone = separate datacenters inside a region.
Scalability is the ability to scale. Elasticity is doing it automatically, up and down.
traps: More nines means less downtime. Each extra nine cuts allowed downtime about tenfold.
Chaining services lowers the overall SLA, and adding redundant copies raises it.
Scaling up has a limit: the largest VM size.
An SLA isn't a guarantee of no outage. It's a commitment backed by service credits.
Autoscale needs rules or metrics, so it doesn't happen without configuration.
revision: Single VM (Premium SSD) 99.9%, availability set 99.95%, across zones 99.99%.
Out and in = instance count. Up and down = instance size.
Elastic = automatic both ways. Agile = fast to deploy and change.
